title: Set up a second sign-in factor
purpose: Add the authenticator app your laboratory requires of your account before you go on to anything else.
summary: Your laboratory requires a second sign-in factor for your account. Set up an authenticator app here; until you do, this session opens only these setup pages.

tasks.title: Set up the authenticator app
steps: Select [[Set up authenticator app]] and enter your password again when asked.
Scan the code shown with your authenticator app and type the six-digit code it gives, then select [[Activate]].
Save the new recovery codes somewhere private, then select [[Continue]]. If you already had codes, they stay and Two-factor authentication opens instead.

tasks.title: Leave without setting it up
steps: Select [[Sign out]]. You are asked again at your next sign-in.

good_to_know: Until your account has an authenticator app, every other page, form and the admin console send you back here.
Continue takes you to the page you were opening when you signed in, or to the start page, and then forgets it.
A shared demonstration account cannot add one. Sign out and use another account.
If you lose your phone later, a recovery code signs you in once; an administrator can remove the old app so you can add a new one.

sections.title: Why you are here
paragraphs: An administrator of your laboratory chose which accounts must have a second sign-in factor on Security settings: every staff account, staff with chosen roles, staff who can view patient information, accounts that can open the admin console, or client portal accounts. Why it is needed names the parts that cover your account as it stands now.
Whether the rule covers your account is decided when you sign in. A rule saved while you were already signed in applies from your next sign-in.

items.label: Set up authenticator app
items.description: Opens the authenticator app setup. It asks you to confirm who you are first (your password, or a recovery code for an account without one) unless you did so in the last 5 minutes. Not shown to a shared demonstration account.

items.label: Sign out
items.description: Ends this session. Nothing is set up; the next sign-in brings you back here.

items.label: Continue
items.description: Shown on the recovery codes page (or Two-factor authentication) once the app is set up: goes on to the page you were opening when you signed in, or to the start page, and then forgets it. Two tabs choosing it at the same moment can both go there.

sections.title: What this session can open
paragraphs: While your account has no authenticator app, this session opens only this page, Two-factor authentication, the app setup, the confirmation it asks for, Sign out and sign-in. Any other page, form, dialog or file sends you back here, and the menu, Find, What's new and the other account pages are not shown. Recovery codes alone are not a second factor.

Once the app is set up, everything your roles allow opens again. If the app is removed later, every session of yours the rule covered at sign-in comes back here at its next request until you add one. If the rule stops covering your account (a role removed, the rule changed), this session goes on without one for as long as that lasts.
